purpose: Elevate the TrinityX360 process to UID 0 before the write bench, to measure whether UID 0 removes the ~1.5 GB per-process write throttle (issue #80). The console runs etaHEN, whose 9028 command jailbreaks by a ptrace hijack that killed our multithreaded process (fix 186b/186c); PATH B is used instead: a bundled one-shot helper ELF is streamed to the local elfldr (127.0.0.1:9021) and elevates the process cooperatively via the ELV1 handshake.

parts.lapy.elf: the owned one-shot elevation helper, built in CI (build_owned_daemon.py --elf-helper --title PPSA83600), bundled at /app0/lapy.elf, streamed to elfldr by the eboot at startup when the probe is on. NOT linked into eboot.bin.
parts.port/vendor/lapy/: the isolated LGPL ELV1/elfldr client (lapy_elevation_client.c + lapy_elevation_protocol.h) that the MIT eboot calls through lapy_elevation_client.h. A separable, relinkable unit; not fused into TrinityX360's MIT source.

prospero_win_client.name: prospero-win (the ELV1/elfldr client our module is adapted from)

license.note: Both the built lapy.elf (owned_root_daemon.c etc. MIT + lapy_elevation_protocol.h LGPL-2.1-or-later) and the port/vendor/lapy client (adapted from prospero-win's LGPL-2.1 native/pw_lapy_elevation.c + the LGPL ELV1 header) are LGPL-2.1-or-later, NOT MIT. TrinityX360's own eboot stays MIT and only calls the LGPL client through its header (LGPL clause 5).
license.corresponding_source: The exact source matching the shipped binary is the upstream repos at the pinned commits above (Lapy helper, prospero-win client), plus port/vendor/lapy in this repository. See tools/source-1.0.2/lapy-daemon/NOTICE.md to relink.
license.relink: eboot links the LGPL client (port/vendor/lapy/lapy_elevation_client.c) as a separable unit; the whole project source is public, so the binary is relinkable with a modified client. The LGPL is never fused into TrinityX360's MIT-licensed source files.

build.client: port/vendor/lapy/lapy_elevation_client.c is compiled into the eboot by canary/CMakeLists.txt

deployment.model: The eboot streams the bundled /app0/lapy.elf to the local elfldr (127.0.0.1:9021) at startup, ONLY when /data/homebrew/PPSA83600/elevate-probe.txt says on (off by default). The user accepted this auto-invocation on their own console.
deployment.status: EXPERIMENTAL on the user's firmware (FW 13.60). Elevation changes kernel credentials; the stability risk is the user's to accept. On any failure the app runs at UID 1 and is never closed.
